lines.text: One urgent email from the boss. One big decision.
Friday, four fifty. Sam in Finance gets an email from Hana, the C E O.
Pay a supplier today, and keep it quiet?
Spot the signs. It's not Hana's usual address. It says pay today. The bank details are new. And it asks for secrecy.
Heh. Nobody questions the boss on a Friday afternoon.
Pay now, reply to the email, or call Hana back on her directory number?
Sam calls Hana back on her number in the company directory.
I never sent that. Don't pay it!
Reporting it to I T Security now.
The rule: call back a number you already have. Bank changes, and payments of ten thousand dollars or more, need two approvers. And report it to I T Security.
Quick check. The email lists a new number to confirm. Call it?
No. Only call a number that's already on file.
Pressure is the red flag. Verify first, and report. No one is blamed for reporting.
